title: Hakko Soldering Iron Repair
subtitle: Hakko fell of my desk and landed on its SD-60LS port
description: I decided to completly replace the existing SD-60LS port after I failed to design a support harness for the damaged port.

PXL_20260925_180415290.jpg: The FX-888DX is surprisingly heavy. When I accidentally knocked it off my desk, it took a direct hit face-down on its own port.
PXL_20260925_181759222.jpg: This is a brilliantly engineered product, neatly laid out and exceptionally easy to disassemble.
PXL_20260925_181947308.MACRO_FOCUS.jpg: This looks like it was chewed up and spat out.
PXL_20260926_094925554.jpg: y initial fix was to 3D print a support harness that wraps around the damaged port to lock it in place. I used the existing motherboard screws as anchoring points for the structure. Navigating all the internal structures meant a lot of trial and error, so I iterated the design in 5mm increments.
PXL_20260926_094932286.jpg: I also designed a faceplate to hide the damage on the front. I used transparent filament just because it was already loaded in my printer, but I plan to reprint it in yellow once I'm sure the fit is dialed in.
PXL_20260926_101653442.MACRO_FOCUS.jpg: This is starting to come together nicely
PXL_20260926_151822147.jpg: I happened to have yellow filament that was really close in color to the Hakko faceplate
PXL_20260926_161128593.jpg: The finial design that I arrived at
PXL_20260926_161128594.jpg: These are all of the incremental designs that I printed along the way.
Screenshot 2026-09-26 at 16.42.18.jpg: Eventually, I tracked down a replacement port featuring a threaded screw mounting system, which will be way more reliable than my 3D-printed harness.
Screenshot 2026-09-26 at 17.04.11.jpg: The shipping cost is a real killer here. I hate paying more for delivery on a few grams of plastic than the actual item costs. I really wish companies would support hobbyists by shipping small parts like this via standard letter mail.
